budget: Part of Alphabet ($258B revenue in 2021). YouTube generated $28.8B in advertising revenue in 2021 alone — a 46% YoY increase.

platform_scale.videos_uploaded_per_minute: 500 hours of video uploaded every minute
platform_scale.partner_program_creators: 2 million+ creators in the YouTube Partner Program (YPP)
platform_scale.annual_creator_payouts: $15 billion paid to creators in 2021 (55% rev-share)
platform_scale.us_gdp_contribution: $25 billion contribution to US GDP in 2021 (Oxford Economics)
platform_scale.us_jobs_supported: 425,000 full-time equivalent jobs supported by YouTube's creative ecosystem in the US

current_priorities: Protect creator mental health and well-being — reduce harassment of creators, especially smaller creators with under 10,000 subscribers
Advertiser brand safety — ensure major brand advertising partners are not publicly embarrassed by platform content or metrics
Prevent coordinated 'dislike bombing' attacks — groups of users coordinating to mass-dislike a specific creator's content as a harassment mechanism
Maintain platform trust — increase creator retention in the YouTube Partner Program by making the platform feel safer to produce content on
Grow YouTube Shorts — compete with TikTok's short-form dominance by growing Shorts engagement metrics
competitors: TikTok (1B+ MAU in 2021, most downloaded app globally, primary short-form threat, never had public dislike counts)
Twitch (dominant in live streaming: ~76% of live-streaming hours watched in 2021, zero concept of a dislike button)
Instagram Reels (Meta, direct Shorts competitor, no dislike mechanism)
key_stakeholders: YouTube Creator Community: 2M+ YPP creators whose livelihood depends on the platform
Advertisers: Large brands paying $28.8B/year who do not want their ad placements associated with high-dislike content
YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim: Publicly criticized the removal on his channel description, writing 'Why would YouTube do this?'
MKBHD (Marques Brownlee): High-profile creator who argued the dislike bar is a 'one-glanceable quality indicator'
Linus Sebastian (Linus Tech Tips): Argued on the WAN Show that the real beneficiary is corporate channels, not small creators
Developer Community: Third-party developers who built browser extensions and analytics tools on the YouTube Data API v3 dislikeCount field
regulatory_environment: Operating under GDPR (EU), COPPA (US — child safety on platform), and FTC advertising disclosure requirements. No specific regulation mandates showing or hiding dislike counts.

historical_context.youtube_rewind_2018_dislikes: 20 million+ dislikes — the most disliked video in YouTube history at time of removal decision
historical_context.bieber_baby_former_record: Justin Bieber's 'Baby' previously held the record, surpassed by YouTube Rewind within one week of Rewind's December 2018 release
historical_context.experiment_start: March 2021 — internal A/B test began hiding dislike counts on a subset of videos
historical_context.public_acknowledgment: July 2021 — YouTube publicly confirmed it was running the experiment
historical_context.api_deprecation: December 13, 2021 — YouTube Data API v3 dislikeCount field made private for public requests
